events.title: Hugh Capet is crowned King of the Franks
events.description: Hugh Capet was crowned, replacing the Carolingian line with his own family. The Capetians and their cadet branches would rule France almost without a break until 1848.
events.html: Hugh Capet was crowned, replacing the Carolingian line with his own family. The Capetians and their cadet branches would rule France almost without a break until 1848.

events.title: Samuel de Champlain founds Quebec
events.description: Samuel de Champlain established a fortified trading post at Quebec on the St Lawrence. It became the capital of New France and the heart of French-speaking North America, a culture that endures in Canada today.
events.html: Samuel de Champlain established a fortified trading post at Quebec on the St Lawrence. It became the capital of New France and the heart of French-speaking North America, a culture that endures in Canada today.

events.title: George Washington surrenders Fort Necessity to the French
events.description: Outnumbered and rain-soaked, the 22-year-old Washington surrendered Fort Necessity in western Pennsylvania. It was the only surrender of his military career and an opening clash of the French and Indian War.
events.html: Outnumbered and rain-soaked, the 22-year-old Washington surrendered Fort Necessity in western Pennsylvania. It was the only surrender of his military career and an opening clash of the French and Indian War.

events.title: Pickett's Charge fails on the final day of Gettysburg
events.description: Some 12,500 Confederates advanced across open fields against the Union centre on Cemetery Ridge and were cut down. The repulse ended Lee's invasion of the North and is often called the high-water mark of the Confederacy.
events.html: Some 12,500 Confederates advanced across open fields against the Union centre on Cemetery Ridge and were cut down. The repulse ended Lee's invasion of the North and is often called the high-water mark of the Confederacy.

events.title: Karl Benz drives his Motorwagen in public in Mannheim
events.description: Karl Benz made the first public drive of his three-wheeled Patent-Motorwagen on the Ringstrasse in Mannheim. Patented that January, it is widely regarded as the first practical petrol-powered motor car.

events.title: USS Vincennes shoots down Iran Air Flight 655
events.description: The US cruiser Vincennes, mistaking the Airbus for an attacking fighter, shot down Iran Air Flight 655 over the Persian Gulf, killing all 290 on board. The tragedy deepened hostility between Washington and Tehran.
